intro: You have arrived at Smintheion, a sanctuary in Çanakkale province from the 2nd century BC. This was the temple of Apollo Smintheus, centre of the cult named in the opening pages of the Iliad, and its frieze is carved with scenes from the epic itself.
history: The temple of Apollo Smintheus was built in the second century BC at Chryse in the Troad. Its cult appears in the opening pages of the Iliad: it is from here that Apollo, answering the prayer of his priest Chryses, sends plague arrows into the Greek camp. The temple's frieze is carved with scenes from the Iliad, a rare case of an epic depicted at its own cult centre.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the temple podium and the Iliad frieze. Then seek out the sacred spring and the Roman bath.
facts: Did you know? The epithet Smintheus means 'of the mouse': here Apollo was worshipped both as the god who kept mice off the fields and as the one who sent plague. And the temple frieze is carved with scenes from the Iliad, a rare case of an epic depicted at its own cult centre.
outro: This brings our tour of Smintheion to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. May the old stories stay with you as you leave. Enjoy your visit.
